name: Burg Bruck
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Bruck in Lienz ? former residence of the Counts of G?rz with a mighty keep, Romanesque double chapel, and Albin Egger-Lienz Gallery.
beschreibung:
Overview

The imposing Schloss Bruck (historically also Burg Bruck) perches on a wooded hill above the Dolomite town of Lienz in Osttirol at an elevation of around 725 metres. As the former primary residence of the powerful Counts of G?rz, this fortified castle complex now houses the Museum der Stadt Lienz. Featuring a 37-metre-high Romanesque keep, expansive castle halls, and a two-storey double chapel, the complex is considered the most significant secular architectural monument in Osttirol, treating visitors to sweeping panoramic views across the Lienz valley basin and the Lienzer Dolomiten.

History & Architecture

Between 1252 and 1277, Count Meinhard III. von G?rz and his sons had this residential fortress built to secure the administrative centre of the G?rz princely dynasty. When the dynasty died out in the male line on 12 April 1500 with the passing of Count Leonhard, the entire County of G?rz passed to King Maximilian I. von Habsburg under an inheritance treaty. Following a succession of noble owners and temporary uses as a brewery and field hospital, the town of Lienz acquired the property in 1942. The art-historical crown jewel of the complex is the Romanesque Double Chapel of the Holy Trinity consecrated around 1277: it houses early Romanesque fresco fragments, the 1452 'Throne of Mercy' by Nikolaus Kenntner, and the world-famous late-Gothic Passion and Marian cycle by painter Simon von Taisten (created between 1490 and 1495). In addition, the museum showcases the largest public collection of masterpieces by renowned Osttirol painter Albin Egger-Lienz (1868?1926).

Visit & Getting There

Schloss Bruck is open seasonally from late May to mid-October: in May, June, September, and October from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 16:00 (closed Mondays); in July and August daily from 10:00 to 18:00 (no closing days). Admission prices (as of 2025/2026): adults ?12.00, seniors and concessions ?10.00, schoolchildren and youths up to 18 years ?2.50, family ticket ?24.00. Admission is free with the Osttirol Card. Arrival by train: ?BB to Lienz station, from where a signposted walking path leads up to the castle in about 25 minutes, or take the city bus to the Schlossberg stop. By car: via the Drautalstra?e B100 or Felbertauernstra?e B108 to Lienz, turn off onto Schlossberg to reach the free visitor car park directly at Schlossberg 1.

Tips

The castle courtyard and the castle caf? on the ground floor are step-free and accessible; due to historic preservation, the historic halls, chapel, and keep can only be reached via stairs. After visiting the museum, take a stroll around the idyllic castle pond in the castle park, which invites you to linger beneath the shade of mature trees. The sun terrace of the castle caf? offers delightful views and homemade pastries.
